description: verify-loops.sh's liveurl() (lines 12-16) extracts the LAST http(s) URL found ANYWHERE in the whole ledger file via `grep -oE 'https?://...' "$f" | tail -1`, not the URL specifically belonging to the newest jsonl record. If the newest appended line in published.jsonl/posts.jsonl happened to omit a url field (e.g. a malformed write from a buggy pass), liveurl() would silently fall back to curling an OLDER url from a previous line and report LIVE, masking the fact that the most recent record is malformed/URL-less. This is a minor but real gap in the anti-fake curl check the FIND-007 fix added -- it verifies 'a URL that exists somewhere in the file is live', not 'the most recent claimed publish/post is live'.
